cases.text:
Hi! I'm Emily from TalentBridge HR. Your profile was selected for a remote Data Entry Assistant position.

No experience required. You only need a smartphone and 1-2 hours a day, and you can earn $350 per day.

The interview is held on Telegram, so please contact our hiring manager via Telegram: t.me/talentbridge_hr

To activate your account you must pay a one-time registration fee of $49, which is refundable after your first week. Only 3 spots left, reply today!

reasons: Enough text to evaluate wording and context.
5 independent indicator types point the same way.
Rule-based analysis only. AI review is not connected in this version.

findings.title: Moves you to a private chat
findings.explanation: Fake recruiters push conversations to Telegram, WhatsApp or Signal, where there is no company record and accounts disappear easily.
evidence: contact our hiring manager via Telegram

findings.title: Unrealistic earnings promise
findings.explanation: Guaranteed profits or high pay for little effort do not exist. These promises are the hook for investment, task and job scams.

findings.title: Job offer that asks you to pay
findings.explanation: Real employers pay you. They never charge for training, equipment, registration or a “starter kit”.

findings.title: Job that sounds too easy
findings.explanation: Offers that need no experience, no interview and pay for trivial tasks like liking videos are common in task and recruitment scams.

findings.title: Asks you to pay a fee first
findings.explanation: Requests to pay a small fee, deposit or charge before you receive a parcel, job, prize or refund are the core of advance-fee fraud.

findings.title: Artificial deadline
findings.explanation: Scammers set short deadlines so you act before you have time to check. Real organisations rarely demand action within hours.

findings.title: Pressure combined with a link
findings.explanation: Urgent or threatening wording next to a link is the core phishing recipe: it makes you click before you check where the link goes.

checks.detail: No protocol was given, so we cannot tell whether the link uses HTTPS.
Does not imitate any of the brands we track.

findings.title: Chase name placed in a subdomain

findings.title: Claims to be Chase

findings.explanation: Messages that threaten suspension, fines or legal action are designed to trigger fear. Contact the organisation through its official app or number instead.
